extracted.intended_audience: academic researchers applying to the William T. Grant Foundation for research on youth inequality or research use (U.S.-focused)
extracted.subtask_short: grant proposals on reducing youth inequality
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and submitting empirical research proposals to the William T. Grant Foundation focused on reducing inequality in youth outcomes or improving the use of research evidence in decisions affecting young people in the United States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Quality and Design
rubrics_metrics.description: External peer reviewers and internal staff evaluate research design, methods, team qualifications, and potential impact. The Foundation focuses support on empirical studies for which applicants have already performed a literature review, identified specific research questions and/or hypotheses, and possess sufficiently detailed research methods and data analysis plans so that reviewers can evaluate their rigor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires clear, rigorous empirical design with detailed methods and analysis plans; reviewers will assess methodological rigor and potential impact. Application components call for detailed methods and analysis plans; pre-tested instruments are preferred and feasibility evidence is required. Methods-pluralistic approaches (qualitative, quantitative, mixed) are acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant Track Record
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation evaluates an applicant's track record based on prior success managing a research project and peer-reviewed empirical publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For certain proposals, evidence of connections with audiences outside of the research community is also evaluated. Demonstrating prior project management, successful completion of studies, and publication record strengthens the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theoretical Rigor and Practical Relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed evaluation studies should specify a theoretical basis for the program, policy, or practice and enhance understanding of its effects, including consideration of mechanisms and examination of variation in intervention effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Studies should shed light not solely on 'what works,' but on 'what works for whom, under what conditions, and why.' Applications should explicitly link theory to hypotheses, measurement, and analytic strategies and reflect on policy/practice implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team Qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior training and publications should demonstrate that the research team has a track record of conducting strong research and communicating it successfully; teams should be well-positioned to address varied tasks and may combine expertise across disciplines or methods with specific value for each member's contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe each member's role and value; show complementary expertise (e.g., substantive, methodological, implementation, communication). Evidence of relevant training, publications, and prior collaborative success is important.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fit to Program Area — Reducing Inequality
rubrics_metrics.description: Research should build, test, or increase understanding of programs, policies, or practices that reduce inequality in academic, social, behavioral, or economic outcomes among young people aged 5–25, specifically focused on race, ethnicity, economic standing, language minority status, or immigrant origins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should clearly articulate how the work targets reductions in inequality for the specified subpopulations and outcomes and how findings would inform policies or practices aimed at reducing disparities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fit to Program Area — Improving the Use of Research Evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Research should investigate strategies to improve the use of research evidence in policy and practice, examine challenges in research-practice partnerships, study how to make research more usable, and test interventions to improve research uptake.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should focus on practical strategies, rigorous evaluation of research-use interventions, and measurable outcomes related to research uptake and use in decision-making contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: W.T. Grant Scholars Program Eligibility and Aims
rubrics_metrics.description: The W.T. Grant Scholars Program provides five-year career awards for early-career researchers ($350,000 over 5 years) to support ambitious learning agendas; eligible applicants received their doctorate within the last 7 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must meet the early-career eligibility window and propose an ambitious, coherent five-year research and career development plan aligned with the Foundation's mission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application Process and Required Components
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission begins with a letter of inquiry; selected applicants are invited to submit a full proposal. Full proposals must include detailed methods and analysis plans; pre-tested instruments are preferred and feasibility evidence is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the LOI-first process; ensure full proposals provide the level of methodological detail reviewers need to assess rigor and feasibility, including pilot data or other evidence that the study can be implemented as proposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological Pluralism
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation is methods-pluralistic and supports qualitative, quantitative, and mixed-methods approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the methodological approach best suited to the research question; justify methods and show how chosen methods will address mechanisms, heterogeneity, and policy-relevant inference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on Research Use and Communication
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation gives weight to research that improves the use of evidence and that demonstrates capacity to communicate findings and connect with audiences outside academia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe plans for dissemination, engagement with practitioners or policymakers, and strategies to increase research usability and uptake; evidence of prior success in translating research for nonresearch audiences is favorable.
